day: Thursday of week 23 in Ordinary Time
text:
There is a quiet wisdom running through these readings about how our choices ripple outward, touching the people around us in ways we may not even see. Paul writes not as someone trying to win an argument, but as someone who has learned something harder than logic: that knowledge alone can puff us up, while love builds us up together. He speaks of setting aside his own freedom—his right to eat meat—not because the meat itself matters, but because his brother matters. His conscience matters. His faith matters.

Jesus echoes this same movement of the heart outward. He does not ask us to love only those who deserve it or make it easy. He asks us to give freely, to forgive without counting, to bless those who curse us. It sounds impossible until we remember what he is really saying: that this kind of love makes us like our Father, who is kind even to the ungrateful and the wicked. He is not asking us to become doormats. He is asking us to become merciful.

Perhaps today there is someone whose conscience is tender, whose faith is fragile, and your small choice—to hold back, to spare them, to consider their weakness—could become the thing that holds them steady. Or perhaps you are the one who needs to release something you thought was your right, for the sake of love. What small freedom might you lay down today, not in defeat, but in love?
